name: Security Model Benchmark - fixed dataset v1

findings.title: SQL string concatenation with user input
findings.code:
query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '" + request.args['id'] + "'"
cursor.execute(query)
findings.explanation: User input is concatenated directly into SQL with no parameterisation, so an attacker can inject SQL.

findings.title: f-string SQL query
findings.code: cursor.execute(f"SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE user='{username}'")
findings.explanation: f-string interpolation puts untrusted input straight into SQL.

findings.title: Unescaped user input in HTML response
findings.explanation: Reflected user input is rendered as HTML with no escaping, enabling reflected XSS.

findings.title: innerHTML with user data
findings.explanation: Assigning untrusted data to innerHTML executes it as HTML/JS, DOM XSS.

findings.title: Fetch user-supplied URL server-side
findings.explanation: Server fetches an attacker-controlled URL, SSRF to internal services and cloud metadata.

findings.title: Image proxy without allowlist
findings.explanation: No allowlist or private-IP block, so internal hosts can be reached through the proxy.

findings.title: File path from user input, no sanitisation
findings.explanation: An attacker can use ../ to read files outside /data.

findings.title: Shell command with user input
findings.explanation: User input reaches a shell command, command injection via ; or &&.

findings.title: subprocess shell=True with input
findings.explanation: shell=True with interpolated input allows command injection.

findings.title: Hardcoded API key in source
findings.explanation: A live secret committed in source code can be extracted from the repo.

findings.title: Hardcoded database password
findings.explanation: Credentials in code are visible to anyone with repo access.

findings.title: MD5 for password hashing
findings.explanation: MD5 is fast and collision-prone, unsuitable for password hashing; use bcrypt/argon2.

findings.title: AES ECB mode
findings.explanation: ECB leaks plaintext patterns; use GCM/CBC with a random IV.

findings.title: pickle.loads on user data
findings.explanation: Unpickling untrusted data can execute arbitrary code.

findings.title: yaml.load without SafeLoader
findings.explanation: Unsafe YAML loading can construct arbitrary Python objects.

findings.title: JWT verified without signature check
findings.explanation: Signature verification is disabled, so any token is accepted.

findings.title: JWT with none algorithm accepted
findings.explanation: The none algorithm means no signature is required.

findings.title: Authentication check that always passes
findings.explanation: The or True makes the check always pass, authentication bypass.

findings.title: Password compared with == in timing-unsafe way, no check on empty
findings.code:
if password == stored or password == '':
    login()
findings.explanation: An empty password is accepted, authentication bypass.

findings.title: Direct object reference, no ownership check
findings.explanation: No check that the invoice belongs to the logged-in user, IDOR.

findings.title: Profile fetched by user-supplied id, no check
findings.explanation: Any user id can be requested, exposing other users data.

findings.title: State-changing POST with no CSRF token
findings.explanation: No CSRF protection on a money transfer, cross-site request forgery.

findings.title: Redirect to user-supplied URL
findings.explanation: Unvalidated redirect can send users to a phishing site.

findings.title: Password logged in plaintext
findings.explanation: Passwords in logs leak credentials to anyone with log access.

findings.title: Private key sent to client
findings.explanation: A private key is exposed to the client, it must stay server-side.

findings.title: Parameterised SQL query
findings.explanation: Parameters are bound safely, no injection is possible here.

findings.title: SQL with constant, no user input
findings.code: cursor.execute('SELECT id, name FROM products ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10')
findings.explanation: Query is a constant with no user input.

findings.title: User input escaped by template engine
findings.explanation: Jinja2 autoescapes by default, so the name is escaped in HTML.

findings.title: textContent assignment, not innerHTML
findings.explanation: textContent does not parse HTML, so no XSS.

findings.title: Fetch from a fixed allowlisted host
findings.explanation: URL is a fixed constant, not user-controlled.

findings.title: URL validated against allowlist before fetch
findings.explanation: Only the allowlisted CDN host is reachable.

findings.title: Path checked to stay inside base dir
findings.explanation: The resolved path is checked to stay under BASE before opening.

findings.title: subprocess with argument list, no shell
findings.explanation: Arguments are passed as a list with no shell, so no injection.

findings.title: Command is a fixed constant
findings.explanation: Command is a constant with no user input.

findings.title: Placeholder secret in example code
findings.explanation: This is a placeholder, not a real secret.

findings.title: Secret loaded from environment
findings.explanation: The secret comes from the environment, not from source code.

findings.title: MD5 used only as a cache key, not for security
findings.explanation: MD5 here is a non-security checksum for a cache key, not hashing a password.

findings.title: SHA-256 for file integrity check
findings.explanation: SHA-256 is a sound integrity hash for this use.

findings.title: json.loads on user data
findings.explanation: JSON parsing does not construct arbitrary objects, unlike pickle.

findings.title: yaml.safe_load
findings.explanation: SafeLoader only constructs plain Python types.

findings.title: JWT verified with secret and algorithm
findings.explanation: Signature is verified with a secret and a pinned algorithm.

findings.title: JWT decode in a test with a mock key
findings.explanation: This is test code with a mock secret, not production auth.
findings.reviewer_note: Contestable label. Labelled false_positive because this is test code with a mock secret. Second reviewer: if this code were in production auth rather than a test, the label would be real, severity high. GLM called it real.

findings.title: Admin check with proper role lookup
findings.explanation: Role is checked from the authenticated session, not from user input.

findings.title: Password verified with bcrypt check
findings.explanation: Password is verified against a bcrypt hash, no bypass.

findings.title: Ownership checked before returning invoice
findings.code:
inv = get_invoice(invoice_id)
if inv.owner_id != current_user.id: abort(403)
findings.explanation: Ownership is checked, so other users invoices are not returned.

findings.title: Profile fetched from session, not from input
findings.explanation: The id comes from the authenticated session, not from user input.

findings.title: POST protected by CSRF token decorator
findings.explanation: CSRF protection is applied to this state-changing endpoint.

findings.title: Redirect validated to same host
findings.explanation: Redirect is limited to the site's own host.

findings.title: Username logged, no password
findings.explanation: Only the username is logged, no credential is present.

findings.title: Public key sent to client
findings.explanation: A public key is meant to be shared, this is not sensitive.
